articleHeadline: Liderança de terreiro de Magé participa de Conferência sobre Hanseníase
articleSummary: Hansen's disease (leprosy) is highlighted in Magé, Brazil, as religious leadership from a terreiro, Pai Paulo de Ogun, participates in Brazil's National High-Level Conference on Hansen's Disease. The event links public health policy with human rights and traditional knowledge, emphasizing the strategic role of terreiro communities in health promotion, equity, and addressing long-standing inequalities affecting Black populations and vulnerable territories. By engaging alongside public managers, international bodies, scientific experts, and social movements, the participation broadens understanding of Hansen's disease beyond a purely biomedical frame, underscoring that the illness is deeply influenced by social, cultural, and territorial determinants that impact early diagnosis, access to treatment, and stigma reduction. The involvement of religious and community leaders in policy discussions reinforces social oversight and participatory approaches toward more inclusive, effective disease responses. Pai Paulo reaffirmed a commitment to a Brazil free of Hansen's disease, without stigma, guided by social justice and health equity.
notes: この記事は政策会議への参加報告であり、ハンセン病の現在の流行状況、新規症例、アウトブレイク、または医療危機を示唆する情報を含まない。ハンセン病は既知の慢性感染症であり、会議開催自体は異常な疾患イベントではなく、むしろ社会的・政治的関心の文脈における継続的な疾患対策の取り組みとして位置づけられる。

articleSummary: Spring 2026 centralized prevention and control campaign for animal diseases was launched by Xiongkou Management District (within Qianjiang area) to curb highly pathogenic avian influenza and foot-and-mouth disease. A dedicated epidemic prevention task force established a four-level coordination framework emphasizing prevention, immunization, and gapless coverage. The campaign uses a "+fixed-point plus mobile+" sweep for mandatory immunization, achieving 100% immunization density, ear-tag wearing, and immunization record establishment; vaccine cold-chain management is in place and catch-up immunizations are underway. Simultaneously, farm areas are disinfected with source elimination, daily surveillance maintained, strict quarantine of introduced stock enforced, and safe disposal of dead animals ensured. Oversight of farming, transport, and trade chains is tightened; violations are cracked down, and vaccination promotion engages farmers. Next steps include tail-end immunizations, antibody monitoring, stronger emergency readiness, material reserves, and ongoing outbreak surveillance to keep the district disease-free and support high-quality animal husbandry and rural revitalization.
notes: 記事はスプリングキャンペーンの方針・対策内容の説明であり、実際の疾病発生事例の報告ではない。鳥インフルエンザは人獣共通感染症として関心対象だが、ヒト感染例、患者数、死亡数などの疫学情報が全く記載されていない。動物疾病の流行性（epidemic-prone）は確認されるが、深刻度や国際的リスクの判断には情報不足。続報の動向監視が適切。

articleSummary: Measles outbreak response in Madiun Regency, East Java, Indonesia, with 16 suspected measles cases reported from January to mid-March 2026. The Madiun Health Office launches a catch-up immunization campaign targeting infants aged 9–19 months who have not completed measles vaccination, from 30 March to 12 April 2026, to be delivered at puskesmas and Posyandu. Health authorities, including survey teams, are intensifying monitoring of under-fives. articleSummary: Rabies-related death reported in Balrampur, Chhattisgarh, India. Ramjit Ram, 35, from Maharajganj village, was bitten by a dog in November 2025 and instead of medical treatment pursued herbal remedies. Although the wound initially seemed healed, his condition worsened on 15 March, and he began producing dog-like vocalisations. He was brought to Ramanujganj Hospital, referred to Ambikapur Medical College, and died during treatment on Monday night. Doctors confirmed rabies as the cause of death. India accounts for a large share of global rabies fatalities: WHO estimates about 36% of worldwide rabies deaths occur in India, with 18,000–20,000 deaths annually; 30–60% of victims are under 15. Rabies transmits via saliva of infected animals, sometimes through a scratch. There is no cure once rabies develops; preventive measures, especially timely vaccination and post-exposure prophylaxis, are essential to prevent spread.

articleHeadline: Estes 11 erros aumentam o risco de infecções alimentares, aponta estudo
articleSummary: As of 2026-03-17, 11 common kitchen practices increase the risk of foodborne infections, according to a University of São Paulo (USP) study published in Food and Humanity. In Brazil, about 5,000 people were surveyed online on food shopping, storage, and handling. Key findings show only 38% properly sanitize vegetables; 17% consume raw or undercooked eggs; and 11.2% delay refrigerating leftovers for more than two hours. These behaviors elevate the risk of foodborne diseases (DTAs), which the World Health Organization estimates affect about 600 million people globally each year. Common symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea, nausea, abdominal pain, and dehydration. The main bacterial culprits identified are Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Salmonella. The study highlights that routine domestic practices may significantly raise infection risk in Brazil, underscoring the need for proper washing, cooking, and timely storage.

articleSummary: First mpox case in Argentina of clade Ib detected: a 31-year-old man in Buenos Aires City, with no recent travel, treated as an outpatient and recovering well. Clade Ib is more transmissible and potentially more severe than previous lineages, and its international spread in 2026 includes the United States, Canada, Brazil, and Mexico, with community transmission in France, Portugal, and Spain. Argentina previously reported only clade II infections; five mpox cases so far in 2026, four in Buenos Aires and one in Río Negro. The Ib sublineage originated in Central Africa and spread globally, though there is no evidence of higher mortality outside endemic regions. Transmission occurs via direct contact with lesions or mucous membranes, sexual contact, contaminated objects, and possibly short-range respiratory exposure. Symptoms include fever, headache, myalgias, lymphadenopathy, fatigue, followed by skin lesions. Argentina’s Health Ministry urges strengthened surveillance, rapid case identification, contact tracing, isolation until lesions heal, and PPE for health workers.
notes: Mpox clade Ibはclade IIより感染性が高く、潜在的にはより重症化の可能性がある。アルゼンチンは従来clade IIのみを報告していたが、今回のclade Ibの検出は疫学的に有意。患者は渡航歴がなく、コミュニティ伝播の可能性を示唆している。米国、カナダ、ブラジル、メキシコでの複数国での確認と、フランス、ポルトガル、スペインでのコミュニティ伝播が報告されており、国際拡大リスクが高い。アルゼンチン保健省が監視強化と接触者追跡を促進している。

articleSummary: Taiwan reports its third-ever Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome (SFTS) case, the first domestic case in three years, as of 2026-03-17. SFTS is a zoonotic, tick-borne infection; domestic outbreak risk is low, though imported cases may occur. Transmission is mainly via bites from ticks carrying the SFTS virus. Incubation is 7–14 days. Common symptoms include fever, nausea, vomiting, reduced appetite, muscle aches, and blood abnormalities—thrombocytopenia and leukopenia—while some patients develop multi-organ failure and death. Fatality rates range from 5–15% generally; studies from Japan, Korea and China report up to 30%, and severe cases can reach 50%, particularly in older adults. There is no specific antiviral; care is supportive. Prevention focuses on avoiding tick exposure during the April–October peak, through protective clothing, repellents (DEET or picaridin), and thorough tick checks with proper removal.
notes: SFTS は東アジア（中国、日本、韓国）で既知の風土病だが、台湾での 3 年ぶりの国内症例は異常性が高い。致死率 30% という高い数値と複数国での報告から、地域的な疫学的重要性が認められる。ただし記事は啓発・情報提供主体であり、新規アウトブレイクの規模については不明。マダニ由来感染症として季節性（4～10月）があり、リスク管理可能性は比較的高い。

articleSummary: In Siberia, cattle are being culled amid reports of an infectious outbreak, prompting street protests. articleSummary: Measles cases in Tokyo rise to 34 this year (as of March 17), equaling last year's total. By March 8, 19 cases reported; 15 more confirmed by Mar 17. Age distribution: 10s (10), 20s (15), 30s (6), 40s (2), 50s (1). Over the past decade, Tokyo recorded: 2017 28; 2018 23; 2019 124; 2020 2; 2021 0; 2022 0; 2023 10; 2024 10; 2025 34; 2026 34 (as of Mar 17). Multiple outbreaks linked to workplaces and schools. Authorities note importations from Indonesia likely contribute; measles spreads when travel resumes. Incubation 10–12 days; initial symptoms fever, cough, runny nose, then high fever and rash after 2–3 days. articleSummary: Yellow fever re-emerged in Venezuela with 36 cases and 20 deaths (2025–early 2026); case fatality rate >55%, mainly adults 10–49. Barinas accounted for about one third of cases and seven deaths, with spread along a jungle–agricultural corridor to Apure, Portuguesa, Guárico, Lara, and Táchira, signaling transboundary risk. Colombia reported imported cases from Apure and Amazonas, indicating active transmission Venezuela had not officially reported. Across South America, January–April 2025 registered 301 cases and 124 deaths (CFR 41.1%); Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia and Peru together had 289 cases and 115 deaths. Apparent CFR >40% in several countries suggests substantial underreporting. Four drivers shape this re-emergence: deforestation and agricultural expansion bringing Haemagogus and Sabethes mosquitoes; climate change lengthening rainy seasons and boosting vectors; migration and porous borders enabling silent spread; institutional weakness and conflict hindering vaccination and surveillance. Calls for One Health and dynamic vaccination models; risk projections extend to Mexico and other regions.

articleHeadline: Measles Data and the Critical Impact of Global Travel on Disease Resurgence, Highlighting the Intersection of Health and Tourism - Travel And Tour World
articleSummary: Measles remains an exceptionally contagious respiratory virus, with airborne persistence up to two hours. Despite US elimination in 2000, sporadic outbreaks and imported cases persist. CDC reports 2024 had 285 confirmed cases; by March 12, 2026, 1,362 cases across 31 jurisdictions, including California, Florida, New York City, and Texas, with about 94% linked to outbreaks. Most infections occur in unvaccinated or vaccination-unknown individuals. Global travel, international airports, cruise ships, and crowded tourist sites drive transmission, with many cases imported by travelers returning from abroad or visitors, including VFR travelers. Globally, outbreaks are noted in Yemen, India, Indonesia, and Pakistan. Measles can cause pneumonia, encephalitis, and permanent hearing loss; mortality is ~1–3 per 1,000 children. Two-dose MMR is ~97% effective; herd immunity of 95% is needed. Vaccination, laboratory support, diagnostics, and travel guidance from the CDC are critical as travel volumes rise and importation risk remains high.
notes: 2024年285例から2026年3月までに1,362例へと急増。米国での排除達成（2000年）後の再流行であり、ワクチン未接種者の比率が高く、国際渡航による輸入症例が主要な感染源。パキスタン、イエメン、インド、インドネシアでの同時流行と複数国への拡散リスクが確認されている。ベクターカテゴリ含有により空気感染リスクへの言及がある。

articleSummary: China's Environmental Protection Bureau, with international scholars, developed a predictive model that integrates climate and dengue virus data to provide up to two months' advance warning of dengue outbreaks (Aedes aegypti) in China. Led by Emilie Finch of the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine and Rachel Lowe of NUS Saw Swee Hock School of Public Health, the study used 2000–2022 weekly dengue data. The model accounts for temperature, rainfall, humidity, Niño 3.4 index, and monthly serotype proportions. Findings: outbreak risk rises when temperatures reach 32°C, with about 30 dry days over three months, during El Niño, or when the dominant serotype shifts in the first two years or after more than six years. Adding climate data increases predictive accuracy by 54%; adding serotype data raises it to 60%. It can forecast eight weeks ahead, and estimates that expanding Wolbachia-infected male Aedes aegypti releases could have avoided ~28% of 2023 cases. Plans include benchmarking against other models and applying to other regions.

In week 10 (2–8 March 2026), 588 HFMD cases were reported, up 38.7% from the four-week average; year-to-date through week 10 total cases reach 6,452. High incidence per 100,000 people was observed in Nhà Bè, Long Hương, and Tân Hải, signaling a potential new epidemic wave as the seasonal shift begins. Doctors note HFMD typically yields two annual outbreaks, with the first from late March to early May and a second in September when schools resume; the March uptick is an early cycle indicator. Transmission is mainly fecal-oral, direct contact, or via contaminated objects; most affected are children under 5. Severe complications can include encephalitis and myocarditis, and death is possible. Authorities have intensified surveillance, school-based monitoring, and public education; residents should practice hand hygiene, cleaning, health monitoring, and prompt medical care for signs.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Detection of a malaria case in Lam Dong Province and the risk of community transmission in 2026
articleHeadline: Phát hiện ca sốt rét tại Lâm Đồng và nguy cơ lây lan trong cộng đồng 2026
articleSummary: On 18 March 2026, Lam Dong Province reported a malaria case in Song Luy Commune, Tiến Thành Hamlet, Di Linh, with transmission risk. The patient, a 32-year-old male farmer, developed fever and chills on 27 February 2026 and was diagnosed at Bac Binh Thuận Regional General Hospital. Lab testing confirmed malaria parasites; he was treated per MoH guidelines and discharged stable. Investigations showed he had stayed in forested Di Linh while coffee picking, returned home with symptoms, and self-medicated; the case is imported malaria. Lam Dong CDC and local health centers tested 53 contacts; all negative. Vector surveillance detected Anopheles dirus, the main malaria vector, in forest zones. Interventions include residual spraying, insecticide-treated nets and hammocks, distribution of nets, intensified surveillance of forest workers and migrants, and public education. Citizens should sleep under treated nets, use repellents, wear long clothing, and seek care for fever.

articleHeadline: Telangana IT minister Sridhar unveils Genome Valley-made TB diagnostic kits
articleSummary: On 2026-03-18, Telangana IT and Industries Minister D Sridhar Babu unveiled drug-resistant TB diagnostic kits manufactured in Genome Valley, Hyderabad, by French diagnostics firm bioMérieux. The kits aim to strengthen India's TB detection and control by enabling early identification of drug-resistant TB, which does not respond to standard treatments. BioMérieux has invested about ₹50 crore in the first phase of its Genome Valley facility, creating around 100 jobs and planning an upcoming R&D laboratory at the site. The event underscored Telangana's growing global role in manufacturing advanced infectious-disease diagnostics. BioMérieux is a global in-vitro diagnostics leader with operations in over 160 countries; the Indo-French Chamber of Commerce and Industry highlighted bilateral trade relations during the event. The article does not report TB case counts or outbreaks.

articleHeadline: Tiba Masa Untuk Pakai Mask Balik Kalau Nak Raya" - Doktor Ingatkan Tentang Bahaya Kes Tibi
articleSummary: TB is rising in Malaysia, with Dr. Syed Anwar warning that tuberculosis can cause permanent lung damage and may spread to the brain or spinal cord, potentially fatal. In two weeks, Malaysia reported about 600 new TB cases; by February 21, more than 3,000 confirmed positives identified. Transmission tends to occur after prolonged contact with an active TB patient, not from a single cough, making crowded gatherings such as bazaars risky ahead of Raya. TB is curable but treatment spans months. Symptoms to watch: cough lasting more than two to three weeks, loss of appetite, unintended weight loss, fever. Diagnostic tests include sputum microscopy for TB bacteria; chest X-ray supports but cannot confirm; TB blood tests indicate exposure but do not diagnose active disease. Dr. Anwar recommends wearing N95 masks in crowded settings.

articleSummary: Influenza B surge observed in recent days, with B-type infections exceeding Influenza A. ENT specialist Li Dianxian reports five B cases diagnosed in daytime clinics, rising to ten influenza cases in one day, nine B and one A. The outbreak appears concentrated among primary school children, with a class reporting more than ten classmates taking leave. Predominant symptoms in B infections include fever, muscle aches, fatigue, abdominal pain, and nausea/vomiting, followed by sore throat and cough. Public health guidance emphasizes hand hygiene, mask-wearing, and avoiding crowded places to curb transmission. The report notes a shift toward B-type predominance but provides no details on infection source or imported/exported cases or lab confirmation methods.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Phú Quốc: Vaccination center overwhelmed after death of a suspected meningococcal meningitis case.
articleHeadline: Phú Quốc: Cơ sở tiêm chủng quá tải sau ca tử vong nghi viêm não mô cầu
articleSummary: One 11-year-old female student, T.H.N.Y., died two days prior in Duong Dong, Phu Quoc; health authorities have not confirmed meningococcal meningitis but are treating as a suspected outbreak and implementing containment. On 18 March, vaccination centers in Duong Dong were overwhelmed as many parents sought meningococcal vaccines. At center T.A (30-4 Street), queues extended onto the street, with parents reporting waits since 8:00; vaccine arrived around 10:00 to meet demand. At center L.C (Nguyen Trung Truc Street), vaccines ran out and staff asked for contact information to notify when available. Phu Quoc Health Center sent samples from the patient to An Giang CDC and Pasteur Institute for meningococcal testing; Pasteur results are pending. Authorities are tracing close contacts, promoting self-monitoring under medical supervision, mandating masks in schools, encouraging vaccination, and disinfecting classrooms as part of outbreak control.
notes: 11歳女児の死亡事例、髄膜炎菌髄膜炎の疑い。検査結果はパスツール研究所で保留中。濃厚接触者追跡、学校内対策（マスク着用義務化、教室消毒）、ワクチン接種プログラムが実施されている。地域内での公衆衛生的関心が高く、親の予防接種センター殺到が確認されている。
